references.text: Balaam had previously refused to go with Balak's messengers, but now he sets out with them anyway after God's permission.
The Lord's angel finally gives Balaam permission to continue the journey with the princes of Moab, but only to say what God commands.
Abraham also saddled his donkey in the morning before he set out, the same action that Balaam performs here.
Peter refers to Balaam as one who left the right way and loved the wages of unrighteousness, and mentions the donkey that spoke.
Jude warns against those who have gone astray on Balaam's path for profit's sake.
John mentions Balaam's teaching that led Israel into sin, a consequence of his journey with the princes of Moab.
Moses reminds the Israelites that Balak sent messengers to Balaam to curse them, but the Lord turned the curse into a blessing.
